title: Bsd Oracle Corpus
objective: Assemble a reproducible independent genus-2/3 BSD arithmetic oracle corpus, validation harness, phase-coverage audit, and WebAssembly acceptance gates without changing implementation APIs

handoff.summary: Added an implementation-independent hyperelliptic BSD acceptance corpus backed by a locally rebuilt official PARI/GP 2.18.1.alpha archive. Six genus-2 rows pin real periods, reduction-gcd torsion bounds, PARI's upstream component-product helper, rank-zero quotient identities 1, 4, 1/4, 9, and 49, and a root-number -1 leading derivative. Two genus-3 period rows and the split J0(33) elliptic-factor identity pin higher-genus analytic normalization. Exact contract vectors separately test r! division, generic dual torsion, principally polarized torsion, basis changes, and subgroup-index-square scaling. The report classifies each plan phase as externally covered, partially covered, self-consistency-only, or uncovered and defines ten concrete WebAssembly integration gates.
risks: No licensed Magma or full SageMath executable was available in this lane. Genus-2 heights, saturation, deficiency, and genus-3 heights therefore remain explicitly without an external numerical oracle; internal bilinearity or refinement tests cannot close that gap.

PARI's genus2tors helper is only a good-reduction gcd upper bound, and its genus2tamagawa test helper is not a Sage.js certificate of Frobenius-fixed rational component classes. The fixture names and documentation preserve those limitations.

The split J0(33) fixture certifies the analytic L-factor identity only. Integral period-lattice, component-group, torsion, and isogeny-index corrections are still required before using it as a complete BSD quotient oracle.

Repository-wide architecture, strict-baselib, and native suites were deliberately left to the integration lane; this fixture-only lane ran the focused verifier, exact PARI transcript replay, syntax, and diff checks.
next_steps: Capture versioned Magma or published research transcripts for genus-2 canonical heights/regulators, a nontrivial saturation, rational component groups, deficiency, and a genus-3 Faltings-Hriljac pairing.
Wire the exact contract vectors and relevant PARI rows into the BSD public API differential tests once the integration API is stable.
Add release-tier pure-quotient and numerical-refinement cases to the shared browser Wasm parity corpus and obtain trusted Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit receipts.
Run the lane-required architecture, strict-baselib, and native checks after integration with the implementation branches.
